svg.text: Rupture Valve & Lowering Valve — the Descent Safety Pair
Rupture valve — the velocity fuse
Normally open, allows free flow both
directions for normal raise/lower.
Closes automatically when oil flow exceeds
rated lowering speed by ~0.3 m/s (~60 fpm)
Responds to FLOW rate, not pressure —
detects a line rupture, not overpressure.
Lowering valve — normal descent control
Electrically operated proportional valve —
meters oil from the jack back to the tank.
Small-increment metering near the floor sill
gives smooth deceleration and leveling accuracy.
Also holds the car stationary — prevents drift
from load-induced pressure when parked.
Temperature compensation
Oil viscosity changes with temperature, which shifts the flow-versus-valve-position relationship —
wide-temperature-swing climates need automatic compensation that adjusts valve opening from oil temp feedback.
Once the rupture valve closes, the car is held safely in place until the fault is corrected — it does not
reopen on its own. Manual reset only.
Two different jobs, two different valves: rupture valve = catastrophic-failure protection; lowering valve = every-day descent control.
